item.title: A2 to Collapse: Transit Traffic Inquiry
item.description: After the accident in Mezzovico, Avanti con Ticino&Lavoro calls for concrete measures to limit the inconvenience of pure transit traffic on the Gotthard axis.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Accident in Mezzovico causes paralysis of the Sottoceneri. - Request the introduction of a border-to-boundary transit tax. - A review of the emergency management plans is necessary.
## Key facts - **What**: Parliamentary question on traffic A2 - When: August 8 (trigger event) - Where: A2, Mezzovico (TI) - Who: Giovanni Albertini, Amalia Mirante, Evaristo Roncelli (Forward with Ticino&Lavoro) - Problem: Fragility of the Ticino road network
The A2 motorway, a vital artery for the Canton of Ticino and for commuter flows to Switzerland, has returned to the center of the political debate after the serious traffic jams recorded on Saturday, August 8. As a result of an accident that occurred in the territory of Mezzovico, traffic suffered a paralysis that involved much of the Sottoceneri for hours, making the pressure on the secondary arteries unbearable. The representatives of Avanti con Ticino & Lavoro, Giovanni Albertini, Amalia Mirante and Evaristo Roncelli, presented a question to the Council of State to denounce what they define as a structural fragility of the road network that is no longer exceptional.
### A road network under stress The August event is not considered an isolated case, but the confirmation of a chronic problem related to the Gotthard axis. The closure of the motorway has caused an unsustainable amount of vehicles to pour onto cantonal and municipal roads, effectively blocking local mobility. The analysis proposed by Avanti with Ticino&Lavoro puts the emphasis on the need for a paradigm shift in the management of cross-border flows. The proposal to introduce a specific tax on transit from border to border aims to make the traffic of pure transit contribute more to the costs and inconveniences generated on the Ticino territory. This economic tool, if implemented, would be a strong signal from the Confederation, called to discuss new solutions to relieve the cantonal road network. In addition to the toll, the interrogation solicits the comparison on alternative measures, such as the restoration of rail solutions for the transport of cars, a theme already discussed in the past but which requires a new analysis in light of the growing congestion.

item.title: A2 paralyzed for hours: question to the Council of State
item.description: Six League grand councillors question the Government after Saturday night from a nightmare on the A2 in Mezzovico with queues up to 13 kilometers.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Question to the Council of State submitted by six Grand Councillors of the Ticino League - Serious road accident that occurred on Saturday evening at the height of Mezzovico on the A2 - Circulation blocked in the north direction with columns up to 13 kilometres between Bissone and the Dosso di Taverne - Full reopening announced more than five hours after the accident, set no earlier than 11pm
## Key facts - What * *: Parliamentary question on traffic management and highway restoration times - When: Following a serious accident that occurred on Saturday night - Where: On the A2 motorway at Mezzovico - Who: Grand Councillors Stefano Quadri, Boris Bignasca, Omar Balli, Raffaella Zucchetti, Andrea Sanvido and Mauro Minotti - Amount: Columns up to 13 kilometres in length registered between Bissone and Dosso di Taverne
After the chaos that broke out on the A2 following a serious accident that occurred at the height of Mezzovico, the formal question to the Council of State is triggered. The Ticino Government was asked for clarification by the Grand Councillors of the Ticino League, Stefano Quadri, the first signatory, supported by Boris Bignasca, Omar Balli, Raffaella Zucchetti, Andrea Sanvido and Mauro Minotti. The central question posed by MEPs sums up the general discontent: does it really take hours and hours to reopen a motorway? The critical event generated a road emergency situation that took thousands of motorists by surprise in ### The consequences on mobility and vehicle blocking
The road consequences recorded following the road accident were defined as very serious by the MEPs who signed the question. Following the impact, road traffic in the north direction was first completely blocked and then only partially restored, while the complete reopening of the motorway axis was announced no earlier than 11.00 pm, or more than five hours after the accident occurred. This accumulated delay in the evacuation and restoration operations has generated massive colonnades that have reached record peaks of up to 13 kilometers in extension, progressively extending along the stretch between Bissone and the Dosso di Taverne. Numerous motorists, including commuters, tourists, families with young children, and the elderly, were literally trapped inside their cars on the highway axis for between three and four hours. This situation of prolonged blockage took place during a day characterized by particularly difficult weather conditions, marked by high temperatures and an influx of particularly intense traffic typical of periods of great mobility. Many citizens thus found themselves unable to leave the motorway, in some cases being deprived of even basic necessities such as drinking water.

The parliamentary group of the Ticinese League has structured a series of specific questions addressed directly to the Council of State to shed full light on the decision-making chain and operating times of emergency management. Among the main points raised are the request to know the exact temporal chronology of the event, starting from the moment of the initial alarm until the total reopening of the motorway headquarters, specifying precisely the time of completion of the health rescue activities, the surveys carried out by the cantonal police, the recovery of the damaged vehicles and the subsequent technical cleaning and restoration of the roadway. It is also formally requested for what technical or logistical reasons it was deemed essential to maintain the closure or the very strong restrictions on transit in the north direction for a period of more than five hours. A further central question concerns the concrete possibility of reopening at least one lane of travel once the health emergencies have ended, so as to simultaneously guarantee the continuation of the surveys and the removal of blocked vehicles. item.title: How dependent is Switzerland on fossil fuels?

item.content:encoded:
Switzerland is a country that imports all the fossil fuels it consumes, with a share of final energy from fossil sources of 58% in 2024. This means that Switzerland is heavily dependent on fossil fuels for its final energy consumption. According to 2024 data, petroleum products such as gasoline, heating oil and aviation fuel account for 45.7% of the final energy consumed in Switzerland, while natural gas accounts for 12.3%. Healthcare work in the Canton of Ticino is an increasingly important choice for healthcare professionals residing in Italy. To pursue this career, you need to understand the regulatory structure that governs the relationship between the two countries. The new tax agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and in force from 1 January 2024, introduced substantial changes in the management of taxation for frontier workers. The Italian ratification took place through Law 83 of 13 June 2023. Pursuant to this legislation, tax at source is withheld only in Switzerland. To avoid double taxation, Italy allows the tax credit to be applied through the EC framework of model 730. It is essential to remember that Switzerland is not a member of the European Union or the Economic Area Analyzing the tax position for a social-health operator who crosses the border daily, for instance through the Brogeda or Gaggiolo crossings to healthcare facilities in the Canton of Ticino, requires attention to recent developments. With the entry into force of the new agreement on January 1, 2024, the distinction between 'old' and 'new' cross-border commuters has been consolidated. For those who were already cross-border commuters before July 17, 2023, a 7,500 euro exemption is provided under a transitional regime covering the 2024–2033 period. For new cross-border commuters, the exemption threshold is set at 10,000 euros. These thresholds directly influence the calculation of net income, as they determine the taxable base to which Italian IRPEF rates are applied. In Italy, IRPEF follows progressive brackets: 23% up to 28,000 euros, 35% for the bracket between 28,001 and 50,000 euros, and 43% for the portion exceeding 50,000 euros.

LAMal is mandatory, and the worker has the right of option, choosing between different deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. This cost is borne by the worker and affects the household budget as much as taxes do. For those who work in the postal sector in Ticino, perhaps on the border, this is an issue that directly affects the workplace.
The Federation of Pensioners spoke of a downsizing of the public service. For those with reduced mobility, the journey to a centralised box can become a daily obstacle, especially in winter with snow and ice, or in summer with the heat. President Bea Heim stressed that universal service must be geared to the needs of all, not just the operational needs of the Post Office.
